sources.title: Bruce D. Smith and Richard A. Yarnell, Initial formation of an indigenous crop complex in eastern North America at 3800 B.P. (2009)
sources.note: Original PNAS 106:6561-6566, DOI 10.1073/pnas.0901846106. Direct PMC is intermittently challenged; full indexed original text retrieved with query site:pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2666091 Riverton occupation. Checked Riverton section, Figure 2 and Developmental Context. Paper explicitly specifies 3800 calendar years BP, approximately 1850 BCE. Family organization is the authors’ interpretation, not a census.

sources.title: Michael Russo, Archaic Shell Rings of the Southeast U.S., National Park Service (2006)
sources.note: Original NPS historic-context PDF directly read on archival mirror: printed pages 31-35 pottery/cooking, Figure 12 on page 32, pages 46-48 mortuary limitations, page 88 Sapelo inventory. No claims adopted from speculative gender assignments or universal first-pottery language. Whole 171-page work counted together.

sources.title: Victor D. Thompson, Questioning Complexity: The Prehistoric Hunter-Gatherers of Sapelo Island, Georgia (2006)
sources.note: Institutional dissertation abstract directly read. Geophysical, distributional, radiocarbon and shell-seasonality evidence; large aggregate population, some year-round residents, and qualified egalitarian interpretation. Later 2022 chronology takes precedence for specific date estimates.

sources.title: C. Fred T. Andrus and Victor D. Thompson, Determining the habitats of mollusk collection at the Sapelo Island shell ring complex (2012)
sources.note: Original Journal of Archaeological Science 39:215-228, DOI 10.1016/j.jas.2011.08.002. Full publisher abstract indexed and read; direct page returns 403. 41 clam and 17 oyster valves; oxygen isotope/salinity comparison suggests broad collection habitats. Authors explicitly cannot estimate precise travel distance.

sources.title: Bronwyn Paige Matlick, Understanding Change in Vessel Technology at the Sapelo Shell Ring Complex (2025)
sources.note: University of Georgia original thesis abstract and metadata read. Late Archaic complex with habitation outside rings; significant vessel-size changes interpreted in relation to group size/environment. This is a master’s study and its social explanation is attributed. No specific educational institution or child pottery exercise claimed.

sources.title: Eduardo Q. Alves and colleagues, Assessing the radiocarbon marine reservoir effect: Cabeçuda shell mound (2023; online 2022)
sources.note: Publisher abstract directly read; original author-uploaded full article text accessed at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366017157_ASSESSING_THE_C_MARINE_RESERVOIR_EFFECT_IN_ARCHAEOLOGICAL_CONTEXTS_DATA_FROM_THE_CABECUDA_SHELL_MOUND_IN_SOUTHERN_BRAZIL . Printed pages 18-19 diet/model and Conclusions: sampled burials 4200-3600 cal BP, explicitly not whole site. Marine fish and C3 plants inferred as major calorie sources; collagen marine percentage not converted to total dietary percentage.

sources.title: Paulo DeBlasis and colleagues, Sambaquis e paisagem: dinâmica natural e arqueologia regional no litoral do sul do Brasil (2007)
sources.note: Original Arqueologia Sul-Americana 3(1):29-61 directly read in complete issue PDF. Abstract pages 29-30, pages 43-45 dated landscape model and dry-ground foundations, pages 53-54 social/memory interpretation. Whole work/issue URL counted together. Regional 6000-1500 BP study used with explicit local scope, no direct equation to Tupi or later Guarani.

sources.title: University of Georgia, UGA study shows resilience of early coastal communities in Georgia (2022)
sources.note: Research team’s institutional account directly/indexed read in full. Source paper DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0258979 identified; publisher page currently exposes metadata/references rather than all prose, so claims here derive from the university account. Three overlapping villages circa 4250-3755 BP; gradual adaptation, lower sea levels/salinity and shrinking oysters. These mechanisms are research interpretations, not one proven cause of abandonment.

proposedOverrides.name: Archaic Amerindian hunter-gatherers
proposedOverrides.summary: A continental atlas umbrella for varied American communities, illustrated through dated homes, native crops, coastal fishing and shell-mound archaeology.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: New umbrella narrative, no shared identities or aliases.
batchIdentityNotes.region: North America is the required single filter value; the record also covers South America, which is explicitly stated publicly. The filter is not a historical boundary.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: One MultiPolygon in hb/borders/world-bc2000.json; bbox [-166.19055,-55.07004,-34.89020,64.83475]. Approximate Riverton, Sapelo and Cabeçuda site points all lie inside. Guana test point lies outside and is not a local case.
batchIdentityNotes.boundaries: No unitary state, ethnic group, migration or shared language inferred. Early horticulture is explicitly included as a limitation of the atlas label. No associations to existing Poverty Point, Valdivia, Andean or living-nation cards.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Riverton circa 3800 calendar BP (~1850 BCE); Sapelo latest study approximately 4250-3755 BP (~2300-1800 BCE), earlier portion partly outside this record; sampled Cabeçuda burials 4200-3600 cal BP (~2250-1650 BCE), not the entire site. Broader regional studies explicitly labeled. No artificial exact item years.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: No secure sentence attributable to the selected communities/centuries established by reviewed sources. Regional pottery surface designs described as visual evidence without a semantic translation.
